name: Velvet Revolution
title: The story of the Velvet Revolution

text: From 1948, Czechoslovakia was ruled by the Communist Party, and no other party could work openly.
People were punished for having supported Alexander Dubček, leader of the Prague Spring of 1968.
src: The Communist Party seized power in Czechoslovakia on 25 February 1948, and no official opposition parties operated thereafter
People were blacklisted for being children of former entrepreneurs / for having supported Alexander Dubček during the Prague Spring of 1968 / Alexander Dubček, leader of the Prague Spring

text: In November 1989, police attacked a student march in Prague.
Students and theatres went on strike, and huge crowds filled Wenceslas Square.
src: A police attack on a student march in Prague on 17 November 1989
Students and theatres went on strike / Demonstrations filled Wenceslas Square and spread to every major city

text: Václav Havel, a writer of plays, founded a group called Civic Forum.
Crowds jingled their keys, a sign meaning “unlock the doors” and “goodbye” to the Communists.
src: Václav Havel, a playwright and human rights activist, founded Civic Forum
Demonstrators jingled their keys, a sign that meant both the unlocking of doors and “Goodbye, it’s time to go home” to the Communists

text: After a two-hour strike by workers across the country, the Communist Party gave up its power.
President Gustáv Husák swore in a government not run by the Communists, and then resigned.
src: a two-hour general strike forced the Communist Party to give up its monopoly of power
Gustáv Husák swore in the first government in 41 years not dominated by the Communists, and resigned

text: Havel was elected president, and in 1990 the country held free elections.
In 1992 Czechoslovakia split peacefully in two: the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic.
src: Václav Havel, a dissident playwright, was elected president on 29 December 1989, and in June 1990 Czechoslovakia held its first democratic elections since 1946
the peaceful division of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic on 31 December 1992
